Houthis strike Saudi oil infrastructure as Riyadh intensifies attacks on Yemen
items.brief: Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis are trading increasingly intense strikes on strategic sites, including oil infrastructure and ports, marking a sharp escalation in fighting between the two sides.

items.title: European Central Bank set to appoint its first Spanish leader
items.brief: The European Central Bank is set to name Pablo Hernández de Cos as its next president, marking the first time that Spain will helm one of the world’s most influential central banks.

items.title: Two Italians killed in alleged Iranian drone attack on Kuwait; Tehran denies involvement
items.brief: Two Italian nationals were killed on Thursday in an Iranian drone attack on the Gulf nation of Kuwait, Italy’s Foreign Minister said.

items.title: At least 31 killed in fuel tanker fire near Cairo, Egyptian authorities say
items.brief: A tanker truck carrying petroleum products crashed in Egypt’s Giza governorate Wednesday, igniting a massive fire that killed at least 31 people and injured 21 others, according to Egyptian authorities.

items.title: The government says Iowa detonation results exceeded expectations. Now what?
items.brief: Two hazy plumes rose over the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant Wednesday morning, punctuating days of legal battles and public outcry over the Army’s plan to detonate nearly five tons of deteriorating lead azide.
